correctness.rationale: Kummer reduction holds identically; a complete compatible-congruence sum yields both p-adic moments and the exact lag covariance. Disjoint divisibility branches yield strict positive inequalities and exclude zero covariance via a valuation contradiction. Prime-adic valuation-depth natural densities produce the rational expression, and stabilization of the floors after depth a plus an exact at-most p^(-a-1) rounding bound proves the Lambert-series limit. The independent checker passed 2,992 direct binomial cases, 68,988 sign tests, several finite positive-lag enumerations, and 569,978 modular moment tuples. Infinite claims are based on proof, not tests.

No matching all-lag sign-density formula appeared.

value.rationale: Positive and negative shift covariances occur at positive densities in a natural fixed Pascal-column divisibility process despite its simple one-point geometric valuation distribution. The new result determines the entire prime/exponent family of those shift-sign frequencies, including exact rational cases and a nontrivial Lambert-series depth limit with uniform error. This is a motivated complete arithmetic correlation invariant rather than an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
